title: SAFe
description: Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe 6.0): ARTs, PI Planning, WSJF, roles and events.

questions.question: Which of these are SAFe 6.0 core values?
questions.explanation: SAFe 6.0 core values: Alignment, Transparency, Respect for people, Relentless improvement.

questions.question: What is the recommended size of an Agile Release Train (ART)?
questions.explanation: Dunbar's number motivates the upper limit of ~125. Larger efforts use multiple ARTs (Large Solution).

questions.question: What does 'PI' stand for in SAFe 6.0?
questions.explanation: SAFe 6.0 renamed 'Program Increment' to 'Planning Interval'. The abbreviation stayed PI.

questions.question: How long is a typical PI?

answers.text: 8–12 weeks, often 4 development iterations plus 1 IP iteration

questions.explanation: A common setup is 5 iterations of 2 weeks: 4 development iterations + 1 Innovation and Planning iteration.

questions.question: What is the Innovation and Planning (IP) iteration used for?

answers.text: A buffer for unfinished work, so the PI can still be met
Starting the next PI's features early

questions.explanation: The IP iteration provides time for innovation, I&A, PI Planning, education and acts as an estimating buffer.

questions.question: What is the role of the Release Train Engineer (RTE)?

answers.text: Servant leader and coach of the ART, facilitating ART events
Lead developer who approves all merges
Owner of the ART backlog and its prioritization

questions.explanation: The RTE facilitates PI Planning, I&A and ART sync. Product Management owns the ART backlog.

questions.question: What does ROAM stand for when handling PI risks?
questions.explanation: During PI Planning, ART risks are ROAMed in front of the whole train.

questions.question: How is Weighted Shortest Job First (WSJF) calculated?

answers.text: Cost of Delay divided by job size (duration)
Business value multiplied by story points
Job size divided by Cost of Delay

questions.explanation: Cost of Delay = user-business value + time criticality + risk reduction/opportunity enablement.

questions.question: Which components make up Cost of Delay in SAFe?
questions.explanation: The three components are estimated relatively (modified Fibonacci) and summed.

questions.question: Who assigns business value to the teams' PI objectives?
questions.explanation: Business Owners assign value (typically 1–10) during PI Planning and rate the actual value at the end of the PI.

questions.question: Which statements about uncommitted objectives are correct?

answers.text: They are planned and use team capacity
They are not part of the team's commitment
They don't count when calculating ART predictability
They are hidden from Business Owners

questions.explanation: Uncommitted objectives absorb uncertainty. Predictability is measured against committed objectives.

questions.question: Which are typical outputs of PI Planning?

answers.text: Committed team and ART PI objectives
ART planning board with features and dependencies
Detailed task estimates for the whole PI

questions.explanation: Teams plan stories for the iterations, but detailed task breakdown is not a PI Planning output.

questions.question: What are the parts of an Inspect & Adapt event?
questions.explanation: I&A happens at the end of each PI, usually in the IP iteration.

questions.question: Which enabler types does SAFe define?
questions.explanation: The four enabler types are Exploration, Architectural, Infrastructure and Compliance.

questions.question: What is the Architectural Runway?

answers.text: Existing code, components and infrastructure needed to implement near-term features without excessive redesign
A long-term architecture document that must be approved before each PI

questions.explanation: Enablers extend the runway; features consume it.

questions.question: Which SAFe configurations exist?
questions.explanation: The four configurations are Essential, Large Solution, Portfolio and Full.

questions.question: Who typically owns and prioritizes features in the ART backlog?

answers.text: The Product Owner of each team

questions.explanation: Product Management owns features (ART backlog); Product Owners own stories (team backlog).

questions.question: What is the target range for ART predictability?
questions.explanation: Predictability = actual business value / planned business value of committed objectives.

questions.question: What does the System Team typically do?

answers.text: Builds and maintains the CI/CD and integration environment
Approves all features before PI Planning

questions.explanation: The System Team is a specialized agile team that helps integrate and demo the solution.

questions.question: In which Portfolio Kanban state is a Lean business case created for an epic?
questions.explanation: Funnel → Reviewing → Analyzing (Lean business case, MVP) → Ready → Implementing → Done.
